mainTopic: Whether רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון accept ברירה, and the rules for pre-written document forms (טופס and תורף) in a גט and other שטרות
overview: The amud opens at the end of רב משרשיא's proof that רבי שמעון accepts ברירה when the outcome depends on someone else, such as a father's approval of קידושין. רבא rejects this distinction. Both רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון accept ברירה in every case, and their strict ruling about wine bought from כותים comes only from the worry that the wineskin might burst. A new משנה then teaches that a scribe may prepare the standard form (טופס) of a גט, a loan document or a sale document in advance. He must leave blanks for the names, the date, and other key details. רבי יהודה invalidates all such forms. רבי אלעזר allows them except for a גט, because of 'וכתב לה', which teaches that a גט must be written לשמה. In the גמרא, שמואל adds that the words 'הרי את מותרת לכל אדם' must also be left blank, following רבי אלעזר. A צריכותא then explains why this had to be stated for several משניות. רבי יונתן explains that writing the טופס in advance is allowed only because of a תקנה for scribes. The גמרא then lays out the גזירות behind רבי יהודה's and רבי אלעזר's rulings, and rewords the source from 'וכתב לה' so that it refers to the תורף.

steps.title: If the father does not agree, the betrothal fails
steps.stepSummary: The last line of the ברייתא that רב משרשיא brought as proof: if the father does not agree, the woman is not betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the father did not want it, she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a ברייתא. A man betrothed a woman on condition that his father agrees, and here we learn that if the father refuses, the קידושין never took effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב משרשיא uses this ברייתא to show that רבי שמעון accepts ברירה when the outcome depends on another person's decision. Whether she was betrothed from the start only becomes clear later, when the father decides. That is exactly what ברירה means.

keyTerms.meaning: wanted, agreed
the father (here, the man's father, whose approval was the condition)
betrothed (married at the first stage, קידושין)

phrases.english: If the father did not want it, she is not betrothed.
phrases.notes: This finishes a ברייתא where a man said 'you are betrothed to me on condition that my father agrees.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא that רב משרשיא cited before this section began.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון accepts ברירה when the outcome depends on someone else's decision.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about קידושין made conditional on the father's approval.

steps.title: Both sages accept retroactive clarification in every case
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects רב משרשיא's distinction. Both רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון accept ברירה, whether the outcome depends on one's own decision or on someone else's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: For both רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, it makes no difference whether a person makes the outcome depend on his own decision or on others' decision. Either way, they hold of ברירה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רב משרשיא. He says there is no need to split cases into 'my own decision' and 'someone else's decision.' Both sages accept ברירה across the board.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב משרשיא had made a distinction so that these sages' strict ruling about the wine would not clash with their acceptance of ברירה elsewhere. רבא drops that distinction completely. That leaves him needing a different explanation for the wine case, which comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: retroactive clarification: a later choice reveals what was true from the start
makes it depend on his own decision
makes it depend on others' decision
there is no difference

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the sages are lenient in the wine case. They are still strict there. He only says their strictness is not because they reject ברירה.

phrases.english: He (רבא) said to him (רב משרשיא):

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֵּין לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן;
phrases.english: Whether according to רבי יהודה or according to רבי שמעון,
it makes no difference if one makes it depend on his own decision,
and it makes no difference if one makes it depend on others' decision;
they hold of retroactive clarification.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ בֵּין לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֵּין לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the distinction that the proof in step 1 was meant to support.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole split between 'own decision' and 'others' decision' as the way to explain these sages' views.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The distinction is unnecessary, because both sages accept ברירה in all cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון accept ברירה whether the outcome depends on oneself or on others.

steps.title: The wine case is about a bursting wineskin, not about ברירה
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains why these sages are still strict about wine bought from כותים. They worry the wineskin may burst before the תרומה is separated, which would leave the person having drunk טבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there (in the wine case), the reason is as it was taught: They said to רבי מאיר, 'Don't you agree that perhaps the wineskin will burst, and it will turn out that this person was drinking טבל retroactively?' He said to them, 'When it bursts, we will deal with it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the real reason the sages forbid drinking the wine right away. They are worried the wineskin might burst before the person separates the תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their question to רבי מאיר only makes sense if ברירה works. If the skin does not burst, the later separation counts from the start. The danger is only that it might burst first, and then no separation ever happens. רבי מאיר answers that we do not worry about an unlikely accident until it actually happens.

keyTerms.meaning: as the reason is taught
a leather wineskin
untithed produce (טבל), forbidden to eat or drink
retroactively, looking back
when it bursts

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, all three sages (רבי יהודה, רבי שמעון, רבי מאיר) accept ברירה. The argument in the wine case is only about whether to worry that the wineskin will burst.
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes how we read the wine dispute. It becomes a disagreement about a practical risk, not about the principle of ברירה.

phrases.english: And there, the reason is as it was taught:
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case of buying wine from כותים, where these sages forbid drinking before the תרומה is separated.

phrases.english: They said to רבי מאיר:
Don't you agree
that perhaps the wineskin will burst,
and it will turn out that this person was drinking untithed produce retroactively?
He said to them: When it bursts.
phrases.notes: He means we only worry about that once it actually bursts, not before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the obvious question raised by step 2: if they accept ברירה, why are they strict about the wine?
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought the sages forbid the wine because they reject ברירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: They forbid it only because of the practical worry that the wineskin will burst before the תרומה is separated.

steps.title: New משנה: pre-written forms of a גט must leave blanks
steps.stepSummary: A scribe who writes standard forms of a גט ahead of time must leave blank spaces for the man's name, the woman's name, and the date.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who writes standard forms of a גט must leave out the place for the man, the place for the woman, and the place for the date.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It allows a scribe to prepare the standard wording of a גט in advance, but he must leave the key personal details blank.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fixed wording may be written ahead of time. The husband's name, the wife's name, and the date must be left empty, so that these details are written later for this specific couple.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה (the start of a new משנה)
the standard forms of a גט
he must leave (blank)
the space for the date

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who writes standard forms of bills of divorce
must leave the place for the man,
and the place for the woman, and the place for the date.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכּוֹתֵב טוֹפְסֵי גִּיטִּין צָרִיךְ שֶׁיַּנִּיחַ מְקוֹם הָאִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It does not depend on the ברירה discussion before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pre-written forms of a גט must leave blank the man's name, the woman's name, and the date.

steps.title: Blanks to leave in a loan document
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues its list. In a pre-written loan שטר, the scribe must leave blanks for the lender, the borrower, the amount and the date.
steps.simpleTranslation: Loan documents: the scribe must leave space for the lender, space for the borrower, space for the money, and space for the date.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from a גט to loan documents and lists which details the scribe must leave blank when he prepares the form ahead of time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like the names and date in a גט, the details that make this loan specific must be filled in later. The general wording can be prepared ahead, but who lent, who borrowed, how much and when cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: A legal document
The lender
The borrower
The date written in the document

phrases.english: Loan documents:
he must leave the place of the lender,
the place of the borrower,
the place of the money, the place of the date.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same blank-space rule from the גט to loan documents.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pre-written loan form must leave blanks for the lender, borrower, amount and date.

steps.title: Blanks to leave in a sale document
steps.stepSummary: In a pre-written sale שטר for land, the scribe must leave blanks for the buyer, seller, price, field and date. Preparing such forms in advance is allowed because of a תקנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sale documents: the scribe must leave space for the buyer, the seller, the money, the field, and the date. This is because of the ordinance.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists the blanks needed in a land-sale document form. It then adds that this advance preparation is allowed because of a תקנה (an ordinance of the sages).
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sale document has one extra blank compared with a loan: the description of the field. The phrase 'מפני התקנה' explains why a scribe may prepare these forms in advance at all. Steps 12-13 show it is a תקנה for the scribes' benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: Documents of sale
The buyer
The seller
An ordinance set up by the sages

phrases.english: Documents of sale:
he must leave the place of the buyer,
and the place of the seller, the place of the money,
the place of the field, and the place of the date;
phrases.notes: Space to describe which field is being sold.

phrases.english: because of the ordinance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the list from loan documents to sale documents and gives the reason: a תקנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pre-written sale form must leave blanks for the buyer, seller, price, field and date. Preparing the form in advance is allowed because of a תקנה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה invalidates all pre-written forms; רבי אלעזר excludes only divorce documents
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה invalidates all these pre-written forms. רבי אלעזר allows them all except a גט, because the פסוק 'וכתב לה' requires it to be written לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה invalidates all of them. רבי אלעזר validates all of them except bills of divorce, as it says 'and he shall write for her', meaning for her sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a dispute about the whole idea of preparing document forms ahead of time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה does not accept pre-written forms at all, even with blanks. רבי אלעזר accepts them for loans and sales. For a גט, though, he says the writing must be done specifically for this woman (לשמה), so even the general part cannot be prepared in advance.

keyTerms.meaning: Invalidates
Validates
Bills of divorce for women
For her sake, written specifically for this woman

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of לשמה from 'וכתב לה' is the key to understanding שמואל's statement in the גמרא right after this.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda invalidates all of them.
Rabbi Elazar validates all of them
except for bills of divorce,
as it says: 'And he shall write for her' –
for her sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After listing the blanks, the משנה brings two opinions that disagree with that first approach.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה invalidates all pre-written forms. רבי אלעזר validates them except a גט, which must be written לשמה.

steps.title: שמואל adds a blank for the key divorce words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with רב יהודה quoting שמואל: a pre-written גט form must also leave blank the key words 'הרי את מותרת לכל אדם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: He must also leave the place for 'You are hereby permitted to any man.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and adds one more blank to the משנה's list for a גט: the central words that actually free the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (step 4) listed only the names and the date. שמואל says the words 'הרי את מותרת לכל אדם' must also be written later, because they are the heart of the גט.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You are hereby permitted to any man', the core words of a גט

steps.confusionAlert: רב יהודה here, who quotes שמואל, is an אמורא. He is not the same person as רבי יהודה, the תנא in the משנה who invalidates all forms.

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
He must also leave the place for
'You are hereby permitted to any man';

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל צָרִיךְ שֶׁיַּנִּיחַ אַף מְקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds one more required blank to the משנה's גט rule in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pre-written גט form must also leave blank the words 'הרי את מותרת לכל אדם'.

steps.title: This follows רבי אלעזר: the core writing must be for her sake
steps.stepSummary: The ruling follows רבי אלעזר. He holds that the witnesses to the handing over (עדי מסירה) make the divorce work, so the core writing of the גט must be done לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the view of רבי אלעזר, who says the witnesses of the handing over make the divorce work, and we need the writing to be for her sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains whose opinion this ruling follows and why the key words must be written specifically for her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אלעזר, the divorce takes effect through the witnesses who see the גט handed over, not through the witnesses who sign it. So the requirement of 'וכתב לה' falls on the writing itself. That is why the most important words cannot be pre-written and must be written לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses who see the גט being handed to the woman
They effect the divorce, they make it work
The writing of the document
We require

steps.whatToRemember: Pre-written גט forms must leave blanks for the names, the date, and also 'הרי את מותרת לכל אדם'. This follows רבי אלעזר: since the witnesses to the handing over make the divorce work, the core writing itself must be לשמה.

phrases.english: And this is the view of Rabbi Elazar,
who says: the witnesses of the handing over make the divorce work,
phrases.notes: He means the witnesses who watch the husband give her the גט, as opposed to the witnesses who sign it.

phrases.english: and we require the writing to be for her sake.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הִיא דְּאָמַר עֵדֵי מְסִירָה כָּרְתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains whose view שמואל's ruling follows and the reasoning behind it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שמואל's extra blank follows רבי אלעזר. Because עדי מסירה make the divorce work, the core writing of the גט must be לשמה.

steps.title: Why the first משנה alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a צריכותא. If we only heard that the משנה about writing on something attached to the ground follows רבי אלעזר, we might still think the משנה about a חרש, שוטה וקטן follows רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is necessary. If he had only taught us about that first משנה, we would say only that one can be read as רבי אלעזר, because it says 'one may not write' and then says 'if one wrote.' But the later משנה, which says 'a גט is made valid only by its signers,' we would say follows רבי מאיר, who holds that the signing witnesses make the divorce work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why we needed to be told about more than one משנה following רבי אלעזר. It starts with the first pair: the משנה on 21b would not teach us about the משנה on 22b.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה on 21b clearly points to רבי אלעזר, because it says 'don't write' but then accepts a גט that was already written. The משנה on 22b gives the reason 'a גט is made valid by its signers,' which sounds exactly like רבי מאיר's view (עדי חתימה כרתי). So without being told, we would have read 22b as רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary, meaning each statement teaches something the others could not
That first one (the earlier משנה)
To establish it, to read the משנה as following a certain opinion
The signing witnesses make the divorce work (רבי מאיר's view)
What makes the גט valid

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of witnesses: רבי מאיר says the signing witnesses (עדי חתימה) make the divorce work, while רבי אלעזר says the witnesses who watch the handing over (עדי מסירה) do.

phrases.english: And it is necessary;
phrases.notes: The גמרא is about to explain why each of these משניות had to be read as רבי אלעזר separately.

phrases.english: for if he had taught us only that first one,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה on 21b about writing a גט on something attached to the ground.

phrases.english: it is in that one that it is possible
to read it as following רבי אלעזר,
since it teaches "One may not write"
and it teaches "If one wrote it";
but the later clause, which teaches
phrases.notes: This is the משנה on 22b about a חרש, שוטה וקטן writing the גט.

phrases.english: "that a גט is made valid only by its signers,"
say it follows רבי מאיר,
who said: the signing witnesses make the divorce work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ruling like רבי אלעזר and explains why it had to be stated for several משניות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה on 21b alone would not show that the משנה on 22b follows רבי אלעזר, since 22b sounds like רבי מאיר.

steps.title: Why the second משנה alone would not be enough either
steps.stepSummary: If we only heard about the משנה on 22b, we still would not know that our משנה follows רבי אלעזר, because its last clause names רבי אלעזר, so its first clause seems to be someone else. Therefore all of them were needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he had taught us only about that משנה, we would say that one too can be read as רבי אלעזר. But this משנה, we would say: since its last clause is רבי אלעזר, its first clause is not רבי אלעזר. So it is necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכותא with the second pair: knowing about 22b would still not tell us about our משנה. It concludes that every statement was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה ends with 'רבי אלעזר מכשיר בכולן חוץ מגיטי נשים,' naming him openly. Usually when a later clause names a sage, we assume the unnamed first clause is a different view, so we would never have guessed the first clause (leaving blanks in a גט form) is also רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a משנה
The last clause of a משנה
If he had taught us (only this)

steps.whatToRemember: Three משניות (21b, 22b, and ours) are all read as רבי אלעזר, and each needed its own statement: 21b is obvious, 22b sounds like רבי מאיר, and ours seems to split רבי אלעזר off into the סיפא.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only about that one,
phrases.notes: Meaning the משנה on 22b about a חרש, שוטה וקטן.

phrases.english: that one too, it is possible
to read it as following רבי אלעזר;
but this one, say
phrases.notes: This is our own משנה about pre-written forms.

phrases.english: since the last clause is רבי אלעזר –
the first clause is not רבי אלעזר;
it is necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן בְּהַהִיא, הָהִיא נָמֵי אִיכָּא לְאוֹקֹמַהּ כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכותא begun in step 10 with the second comparison and the closing word צריכא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each of the three statements was needed, because none of these משניות could be learned from the others.

steps.title: What is the ordinance the משנה mentions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase 'because of the תקנה' and asks which תקנה it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said the scribe may prepare the standard part ahead of time 'because of the ordinance.' What ordinance is that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the wording of the משנה and asks what 'the תקנה' refers to. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allowed a scribe to write the standard part (the טופס) in advance 'מפני התקנה' but never said whose benefit the rule serves. The גמרא wants that spelled out.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic enactment made for people's benefit
What?

phrases.english: "Because of the ordinance":
What ordinance?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the צריכותא, the גמרא goes back to explain the wording of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תקנה permits writing the טופס in advance.

steps.title: It is a תקנה for scribes, following רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן says the תקנה is for the scribe's benefit. The משנה follows רבי אלעזר, who on his own reasoning would forbid even a pre-written טופס, but the Rabbis permitted it for the scribes' sake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן said: it is an ordinance to help the scribe. This follows רבי אלעזר, who holds that the witnesses to the handing over make the divorce work. By strict law, even the standard part should not be written ahead of time. רבנן allowed it only to help scribes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן explains that the תקנה exists to help scribes. He also says this part of the משנה follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר holds עדי מסירה כרתי, so the writing of the גט itself must be לשמה. On that basis, even the טופס should really be written לשמה. The permission to write it in advance is therefore a special rabbinic allowance for scribes, not the basic law.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinance made for the scribe's benefit
The witnesses to the handing over are what make the divorce take effect
By strict law it should be
The Rabbis permitted it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי אלעזר holds that the טופס never needs לשמה. On his own reasoning it really should be לשמה. Writing it in advance is allowed only because of the scribes' תקנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan said:
Because of the ordinance for the scribe;
phrases.notes: The idea is that the scribe can prepare forms ahead of time, so he does not have to rush when a customer comes.

phrases.english: and it is the view of Rabbi Elazar,
who said: the witnesses to the handing over make the divorce take effect;
and by strict law, even the standard form
should also not be written in advance,
but because of the ordinance for scribes
the Rabbis permitted it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן: מִפְּנֵי תַּקָּנַת סוֹפֵר
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a תקנה for scribes. The משנה follows רבי אלעזר, and the טופס is permitted only as a rabbinic allowance.

steps.title: Why רבי יהודה invalidates every pre-written document
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה made two גזירות: no pre-written טופס, out of concern for the תורף, and the same rule for all שטרות, out of concern for גיטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה invalidates all of them. He forbade the standard part because people might come to pre-write the key part. He also applied this to all documents because of bills of divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יהודה in the משנה invalidates every document whose standard part was written in advance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first גזירה is that people may confuse the טופס with the תורף and start pre-writing the key part too. The second גזירה is that people may confuse ordinary שטרות with גיטין. Ordinary שטרות do not need לשמה at all, so the rule for them exists only to protect גיטין.

keyTerms.meaning: He decreed a protective rabbinic rule
Because of the concern about
The standard, general text of a document
The essential, specific part of a document, such as names and date

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda invalidates all of them —
he decreed against the standard form because of the essential part,
he decreed against all documents because of bills of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה and explains it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה makes two גזירות: טופס because of תורף, and שטרות because of גיטין.

steps.title: Why רבי אלעזר forbids only a גט
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר accepts the גזירה of טופס because of תורף, but not the גזירה of שטרות because of גיטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר validates all of them except bills of divorce. He did forbid the standard part because of the key part, but he did not extend the rule from bills of divorce to other documents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי אלעזר's position by showing which of רבי יהודה's two גזירות he accepts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים agree on the first גזירה about the טופס and the תורף. They disagree only about the second one. רבי אלעזר does not apply the rule to ordinary שטרות, so only a גט is invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: Rules it valid
Bills of divorce for women
He did not decree

steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר decree טופס because of תורף. Only רבי יהודה also decrees שטרות because of גיטין.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar rules all of them valid
except for bills of divorce for women —
against the standard form because of the essential part, he did decree;
against all documents because of bills of divorce, he did not decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מַכְשִׁיר בְּכוּלָּן חוּץ מִגִּיטֵּי נָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets רבי אלעזר's view against רבי יהודה's two גזירות from step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר decrees טופס because of תורף, but not שטרות because of גיטין.

steps.title: The פסוק 'וכתב לה' speaks only about the essential part
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's proof for רבי אלעזר: 'לה' (for her) refers to the תורף, so how can it invalidate a pre-written טופס?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה brings the פסוק 'And he shall write for her.' But when the תורה writes 'for her,' it is talking about the essential part!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the פסוק the משנה brought for רבי אלעזר and asks a question about it. The answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'For her' means the part of the גט that is specific to her, which is the תורף. Yet the משנה uses this פסוק to invalidate a pre-written טופס. The גמרא asks how the פסוק can teach anything about the טופס, since the rule against it was only a גזירה.

keyTerms.meaning: "And he shall write for her" (the source that a גט must be written לשמה)
But surely (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: "As it says, 'And he shall write for her'":
phrases.notes: דברים 24:1. These are the משנה's words, which the גמרא is now questioning.

phrases.english: But when "for her" is written —
it is written about the essential part!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כִּי כְּתִיב לָהּ אַתּוֹרֶף הוּא דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source the משנה gives for רבי אלעזר's ruling explained in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's use of 'וכתב לה' to invalidate a גט whose טופס was pre-written.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק requires לשמה only for the תורף, and the טופס is forbidden only by גזירה, so the פסוק should not be the source for invalidating the טופס.

steps.title: Rewording the reason: the verse demands לשמה, and the טופס follows the תורף
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords the earlier explanation. ״וכתב לה״ teaches that a גט must be written לשמה. That requirement is about the תורף, and רבי אלעזר makes the טופס follow it as a גזירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say it this way: it is because the פסוק says ״and he shall write for her," which means the גט must be written for her sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 16 by changing how we word רבי אלעזר's reason. ״וכתב לה״ is not a direct rule about the טופס. It teaches that the writing must be done לשמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed the פסוק itself was being used to disqualify the טופס, even though ״לה״ points to the תורף. The new wording says the פסוק sets up the לשמה requirement, and the Torah states it about the תורף. רבי אלעזר then applies it to the טופס as a protective rule, which fits Step 15: he accepts the גזירה of טופס because of תורף.

keyTerms.meaning: "Rather, say...": the גמרא rewords an earlier statement to fix a problem
"And he shall write for her": the פסוק about writing a גט
For her sake: the גט must be written specifically for this woman
A protective rule made by חכמים to keep people from breaking the main law

steps.whatToRemember: The Torah's לשמה requirement (from ״וכתב לה״) is about the תורף. רבי אלעזר's rule against a pre-written טופס is a גזירה built on top of it, not a direct reading of the פסוק.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is now saying ״לה״ refers to the טופס. It still refers to the תורף. The טופס is included only because רבי אלעזר extends the rule to protect the תורף.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the difference between a Torah rule and a protective rule built around it, and it explains why a pre-written טופס is a rabbinic matter that could be relaxed for the scribes, as in Step 13.

phrases.english: Rather, say: because it is stated
"And he shall write for her": for her sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 16 by rewording רבי אלעזר's reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording of the earlier statement (אלא אימא): the פסוק teaches לשמה for the תורף, and the טופס is included by גזירה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked as if ״וכתב לה״ itself was being read as disqualifying a pre-written טופס, which doesn't fit because ״לה״ is about the תורף.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק sets the לשמה requirement for the תורף. רבי אלעזר extends it to the טופס as a protective rule because of the תורף.
